title: Concrete Short Cap 1-2 Pole
description: Concrete Poles with a 1-2 Alternating Sidearm configuration and a short cap which lies directly on top of the pole are most commonly found in Eastern Cordoba

title: Concrete Up-Facing Insulators 1-2 Pole
description: Poles with a 1-2 sidearm configuration and insulators which stand on top of the sidearms are a good clue to regionguess the eastern plains as they are almost non-existent in Buenos Aires with the exception of a small region on the South coast of the state

title: Concrete Long Cap 1-2 Pole
description: This pole type can be recognized by the top extension being longer than the section between the two sidearms while also having a cap on top of the extension. It is quite rare, however 90+% of the mapped specimen of this type are found in the states of Santiago del Estero and Tucuman - there is a chance they do exist elsewhere too due to its low appearance numbers.

title: Concrete Alternating Sidearm No Cap Pole
description: This type with 3 alternating sidearms with down-facing insulators at the end and an extension of varying lengths at the top of the pole with no cap is by far most commonly found in Cordoba, but is also decently common in Jujuy and Salta as well a Buenos Aires (especially in the South).

title: Concrete Single Crossbar Even Config Pole
description: This pole type with 2 or 3 insulators evenly spread out over a single crossbar can be found scattered across almost the entire country, however is notably more common in the North-West as well as San Luis, Cordoba and Buenos Aires while being rare in the Central Northern states.

title: Metal Fork Poletop No/Short Extension
description: This pole type - characterized by its poletop with insulators hanging from diagonal setup of 2-3 metal bars which can be found on both wooden and concrete poles - in the version where the pole barely goes beyond the intersection with the highest metal bar is by far most commonly found in Corrientes (+ Misiones spill), however does also exist somewhat frequently in Buenos Aires and possibly some of the Western states. This pole is mainly useful to distinguish Corrientes from neighbouring states to the West and South.

title: Metal Fork Poletop Medium Extension
description: This pole type - characterized by its poletop with insulators hanging from a diagonal setup of 2-3 metal bars which can be found on both wooden and concrete poles - in its version where the pole extends a bit above the intersection with the highest metal bar can most commonly be found in San Luis and Misiones as well as Eastern Rio Negro and Chubut and on a few roads around La Rioja.

title: Metal Fork Poletop Long Extension
description: This pole type - characterized by its poletop with insulators hanging from a diagonal setup of 2-3 metal bars which can be found on both wooden and concrete poles - in its version where the pole extends far beyond the intersection with the highest metal bar can most commonly be found in Misiones and Jujuy and more rarely in Corrientes and other North-Western States.
